summary: Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology, philosophy, and art history. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford (1988–1991) under Alexis Sanderson and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pasang Wangdu is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under the supervision of Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner. He was attested as a professor at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences from 2006 to 2014.

Pascale Haag works in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (~1995–2002) at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (until 2002) and Paris Nanterre University (until 2018), and held a post at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales around 2004.

Pascale Hugon is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who taught Flavio A. Geisshuesler. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig researches religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, Ladwig held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger specialized in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning a Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman. She served as Curator at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco and taught at UC Berkeley.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian of China who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1975–1997), the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997).

Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas. She taught art history there (~1984–1991) and served as professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1991–2018).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani works in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zumo Zhou, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

Patrick Jory is a historian who studied at the University of Western Australia and earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Craig J. Reynolds (~1991–1996). He held a post at the University of Queensland around 2008.

Patrick McAllister works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2006–2011) under doctoral supervisor Helmut Krasser, also studying under Karin Preisendanz and Ernst Steinkellner.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist who studied at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Thomas Burrow, and at Penn under Ludo Rocher. He was a department chair at Indiana University (~1984–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (1991).

Patrick Pranke is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under supervisors Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman, and later taught Brandon J. Harwood.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Cornell (~1986–1994), she held posts at Sonoma State University, the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (1997–2002), and California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).
Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul B. Donnelly specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1980–1998).

Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hermann Grassmann (~1870–1876). He worked at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919) and taught Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki.
